recommendations.description: Explore a controlled transfer of quote data from the existing Excel recording step to the legacy quote system. If a supported import or integration method is available and approved, use it to populate a draft quote for John to review before committing. This addresses the reported repeated entry without assuming that integration is currently feasible.
recommendations.proposed_automation: After confirming an approved technical method and mapping the required fields, automate transfer of the entered quote data into a draft or review state in the legacy quote system. Provide a clear indication of transfer success or failure; route failures for manual handling rather than silently dropping or altering quote data.
recommendations.human_control: John reviews the transferred data against the source quote and decides whether to correct and commit it. Sales remains responsible for the accuracy of the source quote.
dependencies: Confirm whether the legacy quote system supports an approved import, API, or other reliable transfer method.
Agree field mappings, validation rules, access controls, and handling of transfer failures before implementation.
risks: The legacy system may not support a suitable transfer method.
Incorrect field mapping or incomplete source data could create inaccurate draft quotes.
The reported workflow is user-reported practice, not independently verified current practice.

to_be_steps.description: Sales records the quote in Excel, as in the reported process.

If an approved transfer method is available, the process transfers the quote data to a draft or review state in the legacy quote system and reports success or failure. If transfer is unavailable or fails, use an agreed manual fallback.

retained_human_decisions: Sales determines and records the quote details.
John verifies transferred data and decides whether it is ready to commit in the legacy quote system.

assumptions: The described Excel-to-email-to-legacy-system sequence is reported practice, based on evidence-001.
The proposed transfer is a design possibility only; the supplied evidence does not establish system capabilities, integration feasibility, or an approved alternative to email.
The manual fallback and any change to the current handoff require organizational agreement.

verifications.explanation: The user-reported evidence supports the problem this recommendation addresses: quote data is entered in Excel and then manually entered again in the legacy system, with an email handoff. The recommendation appropriately makes implementation conditional on confirming those dependencies, so its rationale is supported but feasibility and readiness are not.

recommendations.title: Create a structured quote submission and transfer
recommendations.description: Replace the reported Excel-to-email handoff and repeated manual transcription with a structured quote submission that can populate the legacy quote system. Treat this as a proposed future design, not as an existing system capability or current practice.
recommendations.proposed_automation: Provide a structured quote intake and, if the legacy system supports it, automatically validate and transfer submitted quote fields into a draft or staging record. Route validation failures or unsupported fields for human resolution rather than silently dropping them.
recommendations.human_control: John reviews the transferred quote and resolves exceptions before committing it to the legacy system.
dependencies: Confirm that the legacy quote system supports a suitable import, API, or other controlled entry mechanism.
Decide which quote fields are required and which system or record is authoritative.
Approve the structured intake and exception-handling process.
risks: A transfer could omit or mis-map quote data if field definitions are incomplete.
The legacy system may not support a practical automated transfer; a different design would then be needed.
Changing the intake method before agreeing on the authoritative record could create inconsistent quote records.

recommendations.title: Use automated completeness checks and exception routing
recommendations.description: Add checks to the proposed structured submission so incomplete or invalid data is identified before it reaches the legacy system, reducing avoidable rework without automating quote judgment.
recommendations.proposed_automation: Subject to agreement on required fields and validation rules, automatically check submissions for completeness and format, then route failures to Sales for correction and successful submissions to the transfer and review process.
recommendations.human_control: Sales corrects flagged information; John retains responsibility for reviewing the quote before final commitment.
dependencies: Agree and document the required fields and validation rules.
Determine how corrected submissions and their revisions will be handled.
risks: Rules that are incomplete or too restrictive could flag valid quotes or allow errors through.
Automated checks cannot replace human judgment about quote content.

to_be_steps.description: Sales prepares a quote using the approved structured intake. Whether Excel remains available as an input or is replaced must be decided before implementation.
The intake checks agreed completeness and formatting rules; submissions with issues are returned to Sales for correction.
If a supported legacy-system transfer mechanism is available, the validated submission populates a draft or staging record; otherwise, the transfer design must be revisited rather than assumed.
John reviews the transferred quote, resolves exceptions, and commits it to the legacy system.

retained_human_decisions: Sales prepares and corrects quote information.
John reviews the quote and decides whether it is ready to commit to the legacy system.
The organization decides which record is authoritative and whether Excel remains part of the future process.
assumptions: A structured intake and automated transfer are proposed design possibilities, not capabilities established by the supplied evidence.
The reported Excel, email, and manual-entry process is user-reported practice; no supplied document establishes it as policy or procedure.
The proposed process assumes the organization approves required-field rules and an acceptable way to transfer data into the legacy system.
